crime_highlights: Mr. Power raced forward with Mr. Gannon and they each punched Mr. Ward in the area of his face, which knocked Mr. Ward to the ground
Mr. Power remained on top of him and punched him two or three more times
the second co-accused [Mr. Brushett] intervened by forcefully kicking Mr. Ward in the head while he lay motionless on the ground
Mr. Power casually walked away from the victim who was lying on the pavement motionless and unconscious
Mr. Ward was beaten into unconsciousness by himself, Mr. Brushett and Mr. Gannon
they found Mr. Ward laying on the ground, unconscious, bleeding from his nose and mouth
rationale_highlights: Mr. Power is a youthful, Aboriginal offender
The redacted Gladue Report contains several systemic and personal Gladue factors for the Court to consider in mitigation of Mr. Power’s moral culpability for the offences before the Court
note: Court's conclusion brief; later para 88 also cites Gladue factors in setting lower end.

crime_highlights: he wrote a note saying: he wanted hydromorphone, robbery, he didn’t want violence
He got the drugs and walked out of the store, not rushing.
Mr. Syliboy wanted to be arrested so he would be held at the Burnside Correctional Facility
Either way, the victim noted her concern for the potential for violence.
rationale_highlights: his moral culpability is reduced given his distrust and alienation from this system, resultant from his experiences as an Indigenous person and the colonial history of the system itself
Mr. Syliboy’s past is one of trauma that he needs to keep addressing.
his moral culpability is reduced considering his life circumstances as an Indigenous person
These are direct reflections of the impact of colonialism and racism on Indigenous communities.

crime_highlights: Mr. Ryan emerged and confronted Mr. Corbett, accusing him of taking his liquor
At this point the accused produced a knife and stabbed Mr. Corbett in the left groin area.
He felt the blood on his pants.
It immediately disabled him, and he collapsed.
rationale_highlights: should the perpetrator of the harm done to Mr. Corbett be punished any less, or in any different way, because the perpetrator is of aboriginal ancestry?

such hardships and deprivations, while not unique to individual indigenous persons, were visited wholesale upon them as a people. They were largely the result of laws and policies which were formed and animated by racism.

this court and society at large must try to understand how Mr. Ryan’s upbringing, how his experience as an indigenous person in a society which marginalized and humiliated Mi’kmaq people may have contributed to Rein’s actions on the night in question
note: Court hedges; never clearly states reduced culpability, sentence 4 months outside usual range.
